physicalNotes: Radius 0.23641757 Jupiter radii from Magliano et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.519.1562M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.519.1562M/abstract): 16,902 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0236 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 3.99344182705 d
sources.shape: Magliano et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.519.1562M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAGLIANO_ET_AL_2023): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0269 au and stellar radius 0.362 solar radii; Magliano et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.519.1562M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAGLIANO_ET_AL_2023): inclination 88.9 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2458385.036312 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 8 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
